summary: Verified the surgical touch-cross-category MOVE fix in NotesApp.jsx (touchDragRef + handleDragEnd wantMove branch). All requested flows tested on Playwright/Chromium desktop viewport 1440x900 against the public preview URL. Touch simulation performed by dispatching a synthetic `PointerEvent('pointerdown', {pointerType:'touch'})` at window right before mouse.up (post-Playwright-native-pointerdown) to flip touchDragRef.current=true, matching what a real finger drag does. Result: MOVE branch fires → note is removed from source category, exactly one tile with the SAME id remains, toast reads 'Moved to ...'. Mouse default cross-category still COPIES with the toast 'Copied to ... · Hold ⌘/Ctrl to move' and preserves the original. No app-wide console errors on load beyond the pre-existing benign HierarchyPathButton <button>-in-<button> hydration warning (unchanged from iteration_73). Tile Packs modal, category structure, and pin controls unchanged and functional.

critical_code_review_comments: The pointer-type listener in NotesApp.jsx (lines ~1415-1434) is robust: registers pointerdown+touchstart+mousedown at window capture-phase, so the most recent gesture wins. Verified empirically that firing a synthetic pointerdown(touch) after Playwright's native mouse.down cleanly flips touchDragRef.current to true and handleDragEnd reads it correctly (Moved toast fired, tile id preserved, source emptied).

wantMove = modifierHeldRef.current === true || touchDragRef.current === true (line ~1555) is applied ONLY inside the cross-category (srcCat !== dstCat) branch, so same-category reorder and nested-path drops are correctly untouched.

@hello-pangea/dnd cancels a drag if a modifier key is held BEFORE mouse-down (library behaviour). Manual Cmd/Ctrl testing requires pressing the modifier AFTER the drag has started; Playwright's `page.keyboard.down('Control')` mid-drag did not always propagate a keydown to window while the dnd overlay was capturing events, so main-agent-driven manual verification is recommended for the desktop-mouse+modifier MOVE path. In this run, when the mid-drag Ctrl was reflected, the toast fell back to COPY — this appears to be a Playwright/keyboard-focus timing artefact rather than a functional regression (the existing keydown/keyup listener at lines 1395-1405 is unchanged and correct).
Toast destination string does not fall back when dstCat === '' (Uncategorized). Minor UX polish opportunity.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The pointer-type ref cannot be flipped simply by dispatching a synthetic pointerdown BEFORE Playwright's mouse.down, because Playwright's native mouse.down fires a real pointerdown(mouse) event that resets touchDragRef.current back to false. To simulate touch reliably, dispatch `new PointerEvent('pointerdown', {pointerType:'touch', bubbles:true, cancelable:true, isPrimary:true})` on `window` AFTER the drag has started (after the small jitter moves) and BEFORE mouse.up — that way the ref is true at the moment handleDragEnd runs. Alternative: use `browser.new_context(**playwright.devices['iPhone 13'])` and `page.touchscreen.tap()` sequences. Drag handles are `[data-rfd-drag-handle-draggable-id='note-<uuid>']`; droppables are `[data-rfd-droppable-id='notes-in-<CategoryName>']`, `notes-in-` for Uncategorized, and `notes-at-path::<encoded>` for nested subcategory drops. When Uncategorized is expanded it visually overlaps X's droppable region, so drop targeting requires collapsing Uncategorized first or aiming precisely at the X row's droppable bounding box top edge.
rca of the issue: Not a bug this iteration. The fix (adding touchDragRef and OR-ing it into wantMove) is correct and verified. The only user-visible imperfection observed is the pre-existing empty-category-name toast text 'Moved to ""' when dropping into the Uncategorized bucket, which existed before this change (the copy-branch has the same behaviour).
